description.text: A thousand years ago our ancestors lived in the Gnomish Newlands under the banners of the glorious Gnomish Hierarchy, when the Dragons awoke, causing countless kobolds to rise up and destroy many of our cities and forcing us to flee from what is now called the 'Dragon Coast'. We spent centuries wandering from country to country until we finally settled in Esmaria. Of course, during our migration we learned how to efficiently move a large group of people through the countryside...

We spent centuries wandering from country to country until we finally settled in Esmaria. Of course, during our migration we learned how to efficiently move a large group of people through the countryside...

description.text: We have been in Esmaria for centuries, in that time it is only natural that we adopted some of the customs of our saviours, including their religion. To make our ties with our neighbours even stronger, Giberd can also count a bustling human minority as part of its citizenry, with them being able to elect representatives for the city council. We are as Esmari as anyone.

description.text:
No day is of greater importance to a Giberdi gnome then Gibing Day. The festival has occurred since the day Giberd was founded, repeating on the same day every year since.
The festival starts with the ringing of church bells as denizens gather in their town squares; from there, a human is randomly selected from the crowd to play the role of the King of Esmaria and a gnome to play the gnomish delegate.
Each signs a small piece of paper, reflecting the historical transfer of Giberd to the gnomes. They then initiate the first dance together, gnomes pairing up with humans in a grand circle around the two actors, gnome arms linked with human as the celebrations continue.

Finally, a feast is prepared in the town centre, with a mix of traditional gnomish & Esmari dishes. All partake in the feast and watch from the river the passing of a procession of gnomish ships. These decorative ships are rebuilt and floated each year, to commemorate how the gnomish refugees entered Giberd and called it home.

description.text: When people mention the gnomes, the first thing that comes to their minds is our craftsmanship. Though our permanence in Esmaria has modified our way of life, we still have our skills. Recently, though, there have been cities which, thanks to the riches of the new world, have expanded greatly. Some of the gnomish scholars in Konwell have returned with the idea to institute a dedicated urbanistic engineering academy which will serve us well in keeping up with the rest of the world.

description.text:
The drink of choice of the river parties for more than a hundred years, Golden Giberdi is the peak of luxurious liquor. Sold in a gnome-shaped bottle expertly crafted by Giberdi glassblowers and wrapped in decadent gold leaf from the minted gold coins of the Empire of Anbennar, it fetches a premium at home and abroad.
Lapping luxury from the tip of the gnome's hat, which softly uncorks to reveal the luscious liquid inside, few will be left standing after a glass or two of this beautiful booze.
While some may claim that the high alcohol content of Golden Giberdi is the prime reason so many accidents occur at our river parties, Glibgear’s Golden Brewery laugh at such petty calumny.
So pour a glass of Golden Giberdi fast and steer your party in the right direction.

description.text: The discoveries brought home from Aelantir truly changed the world as we know it, from religion to, of course, technology. Some of our adventurers brought home several 'souvenirs' from the ancestral home of the elves, and those souvenirs are the joy of our engineers, who have basically gone crazy with experiments. By setting a desolated area dedicated to these experiments, we may at least not destroy our city, we may at least protect our city from their mad machinations.

description.text: Gnomes aren't renowned for their physical prowess. We always had to use over encumbering machinery to lift weights that humans are able to lift with their bare hands, and they too have limits, not wanting to work all day long like all gnomes. Our master engineers, though, have finally developed an exoskeleton that can be worn by gnomes, maybe even making larger ones for our human companions, that make us able to lift and transport cargo that we didn't even think was able to be moved in the first place.

player_overview.avoid_if: You do not want to manage dense internal politics and an artificery campaign. Ravellian policy can change with future elections.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Balance three faction influences, elections, and research rewards; begin with a magic-and-artifice mix, then deepen institutions, research, and the God Fragment.
player_overview.overview: Giberd is a free city where gnomish research, commerce, and imperial politics share the same table. Manage three factions with different positions on technology, institutions, and religious groups; artificery is the axis of research, maintenance, and political competition.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy artificer research, factions, and imperial politics.

values.rationale: Research, commerce, and institutional development provide public benefits, while treatment under the Ravellian system may improve or become more restrictive depending on policy. Compared with the Glass Lords' baseline value of 73 and Reveria's 66, this falls near the lower end of the good spectrum rather than receiving an idealised maximum. Exclusion of artificers is not proof of purges or enslavement; imperial ambition and artificery alone do not determine good or evil. Policy choices have separate limits, and reversible choices are not presented as permanent moral outcomes.
